security_frame.attacker: A physical attacker able to inject a single-bit fault into a multi-bit configuration signal in flight, which is the exact threat model the strict multi-bit test exists to defeat.
security_frame.precondition: A security-critical configuration field is encoded as MuBi4False (4'h9), the disabled state, and is being checked by mubi4_test_true_strict before a countermeasure is bypassed or an interface is enabled.
security_frame.input: One bit flip on the four-bit bus, or one write of the encoding 4'h7 by software into a MuBi4 register field.
security_frame.protected_asset: The single-bit-fault detection guarantee of the MuBi4 encoding, and every countermeasure that depends on it (the SEC_CM: CONFIG.MUBI markers in the tree).
security_frame.security_property: mubi4_test_true_strict must return true for exactly one encoding, MuBi4True (4'h6). That exactness is the entire reason the strict variant exists alongside the loose one: MuBi4True and MuBi4False are bitwise complements, so no single bit flip can turn one into the other, and accepting only the exact value means any single-bit fault is rejected.
security_frame.modification: In caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg.sv the four-bit strict true test at caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg.sv:46-50 was rewritten from an exact comparison into a Hamming-distance test: it XORs the input with MuBi4True and accepts a delta of 4'h0 or 4'h1. That widens the accepted set from one encoding to two, so the encoding 4'h7 is also accepted.

security_feature_bypassed: The single-bit-fault detection property of the strict MuBi4 true test, on which the tree's SEC_CM: CONFIG.MUBI countermeasures depend
proof_goal: Show that the four-bit strict test accepts an encoding other than MuBi4True, that the same package declares that encoding invalid, that the package's other three widths and a second multi-bit package in the same tree implement the exact comparison, and that restoring the exact comparison makes the same testbench reject the claim.

proof_style.primary: structural audit of the audited RTL against its own other instances and its own contract
secondary: exhaustive directed simulation over all 16 four-bit encodings with cover counters
negative control on a patched scratch copy

minimum_attack_sequence: A MuBi4 configuration field sits at MuBi4False (4'h9), the disabled encoding, or at any other value the strict test should reject.
The attacker perturbs the bus so it reads 4'h7, either by injecting a single-bit fault or, where the field is software-writable, by writing that encoding directly.
mubi4_test_true_strict(4'h7) returns true, because 4'h7 ^ 4'h6 == 4'h1 and the rewritten test accepts a delta of 1.

The consumer treats the configuration as enabled. In csrng_core.sv this is the CONFIG.MUBI countermeasure path: cs_enable_fo, sw_app_enable_pfe and read_int_state_pfe are all derived from this function.

The same package's mubi4_test_invalid(4'h7) also returns true, so the design simultaneously grants the permission and classifies the encoding as a fault, and the fault-alert path and the permission path disagree.
expected_evidence: caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg.sv:46-50 computes delta = val ^ MuBi4True and returns delta inside {4'h0, 4'h1}, rather than comparing for equality.

In-file control: the same package's 8-, 12- and 16-bit strict true tests at caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg.sv:181, :313 and :445 all use an exact equality comparison, and the 4-bit strict false test at :56 does too.

In-file control: a computed census over the package finds 4 strict-true declarations, 3 of which use exact equality and exactly 1 of which uses the delta form, with the two counts summing to the declaration count so a regex miss cannot pass silently.

In-file contract: the three-line comment describing the exact-match requirement survives above the 8-, 12- and 16-bit tests at :177-179, :309-311 and :441-443, but above the 4-bit test at :45 it has been replaced by a one-line comment.

In-file contract: caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg.sv:33 asserts statically that MuBi4True == ~MuBi4False, which is the property the exact test converts into single-bit-fault detection and which the delta test discards.

In-file contradiction: caliptra_prim_mubi_pkg.sv:37 defines mubi4_test_invalid as anything not in {MuBi4True, MuBi4False}, so the package itself declares 4'h7 invalid while the strict test accepts it.
Tree-level control: abr_prim_mubi_pkg.sv:44 in the same tree implements the same four-bit strict true test with the same encoding as an exact comparison, and no delta form appears anywhere in it.

Consumer reachability: a computed census finds the function used at consumer sites across src/, including four SEC_CM: CONFIG.MUBI countermeasure sites in csrng_core.sv whose encodings come from software-writable register fields.
In simulation, an exhaustive sweep of all 16 four-bit encodings shows the strict test accepting 2 of them, the extra one at Hamming distance 1 from MuBi4True.
With the exact comparison restored in a scratch copy, the same sweep accepts exactly 1 encoding, both defect cover counters fall to zero, and the self-checks fail.
success_criteria: Every structural gate holds, including the computed censuses over strict-true declarations and consumer sites.
The exhaustive simulation shows more than one accepted encoding, and shows the extra encoding is one the same package reports as invalid.
The negative control fails on corrected RTL with both defect covers at zero, while the harness's own control observations still pass.

The finding is anchored on the audited tree's own other widths, its own contract comments, its own invalid-encoding test and a second multi-bit package inside the same tree, not on any external comparison.
